title: The disc becomes a pear

objective.text: Describe how the embryonic disc changes shape during week 3.

body.general: Why does the round disc turn into a pear? It grows from about 0.2 mm around day 15 to over 1 mm by day 18 [f4]. Most of the growth is at the head end, fed by cells streaming forward from the streak (the groove where cells move in) [f2]. So the disc becomes broad at the head end and narrow at the tail end [f1]. The head end starts forming its parts in mid-week 3, while the tail end keeps gastrulating (making new layers) until the end of week 4 [f3].
body.mbbs: Over week 3 the round disc stretches into a pear, wide at the head end and slim at the tail [f1]. Growth is mainly cranial, supplied by cells migrating forward from the streak; the streak region stays about the same size [f2]. The disc grows from about 0.2 mm at days 14–15 to about 1.25 mm by day 18 [f4]. Cranial structures begin to differentiate by mid-week 3, while gastrulation continues caudally until the end of week 4 [f3]. Development therefore runs in a cranial-to-caudal direction [f5].

facts.text: The flat, nearly round disc grows into a pear shape: broad at the head end, narrow at the tail end.
Most growth is at the head end, fed by cells streaming forward from the streak; the streak region stays about the same size.
Head structures start to form in mid-week 3, while the tail end is still gastrulating until the end of week 4.
So the embryo develops head end first.
The disc grows from about 0.2 mm on days 14–15 to about 1.25 mm by day 18.
The neural tube is broad at the head end, where it makes the brain, and narrow caudally, where it makes the spinal cord.

misconceptions.wrong: Gastrulation is over by the end of week 3.
misconceptions.right: It goes on at the tail end until the end of week 4.

misconceptions.wrong: The disc grows evenly all over.
misconceptions.right: Most growth is at the head end; the streak region stays about the same size.

checks.prompt: Which day is this disc? Judge by its shape and its size against the ruler, which is 1 mm long.
checks.alt: A small, nearly round disc, about a fifth of a millimetre long against the ruler, with a short streak at one end.
checks.why: Around day 15 the disc is only about 0.2 mm long, with a short streak; by day 18 it is over 1 mm.

checks.prompt: By the end of week 3, what shape is the disc?
options: Broad at the head end, narrow at the tail end
Broad at the tail end, narrow at the head end
checks.why: By the end of week 3 the disc is pear-shaped: wide at the head end, narrow at the tail end.

checks.prompt: Why does the head end of the disc become broad?
options: Most new cells stream forward from the streak to the head end
The disc folds over at the head end
checks.why: Cells pour forward from the streak, so the head end grows most while the streak region stays about the same size.

checks.prompt: Is the disc's shape change finished by the end of week 3?
options: No: the tail end is still gastrulating until the end of week 4
Yes: the tail end finishes first
checks.why: The head end starts forming its parts in mid-week 3, but the tail end keeps gastrulating until the end of week 4.

adult: The broad head end carries the wide front of the future nervous system, which becomes the brain [f6].

remember.q: Why does the disc become pear-shaped?
remember.a: Most growth is at the head end, fed by cells from the streak [f2].

remember.q: How long does gastrulation go on at the tail end?
